title: GitHub - bipinKrishnan/rss_feed: Lightweight dependency-free RSS reader
excerpt: Lightweight dependency-free RSS reader. Contribute to bipinKrishnan/rss_feed development by creating an account on GitHub.
content_html:
A small, dependency-free RSS reader. Paste a link, get a clean place to read.

Warning

This project is vibecoded with DeepSeek.

What it is

Reader is a local web app that turns RSS, Atom and JSON feeds into a three-pane reading experience: your feeds on the left, headlines in the middle, the article on the right. It runs on Node.js with no npm dependencies and no build step — the whole thing is about 3,000 lines of plain JavaScript, HTML and CSS.

  • No accounts, no cloud, no analytics. Everything stays in a JSON file on your machine.
  • No CORS problems: the server fetches feeds, not your browser.
  • No full-text extraction or scraping: it shows what the feed publishes, plus a link to the original.

Features

  • Paste anything: RSS 2.0, RSS 1.0/RDF, Atom, JSON Feed, or a normal website URL (it finds the feed with <link rel="alternate"> autodiscovery).
  • Three-pane reader with responsive layout down to phone width.
  • Light and dark themes, following your system by default.
  • Unread and starred articles, per-feed unread badges, mark-all-read.
  • Search the current view by title, summary or source.
  • Readable articles: full feed content rendered with book-like typography inside a sandboxed iframe. “Open original” is always one click away.
  • Polite fetching: caches feeds, sends ETag / If-Modified-Since, and refreshes stale feeds in the background every 10 minutes.
  • Keyboard-first navigation (see the shortcut table below).
  • Zero dependencies: just node server.js.

Quick start

Requires Node.js 20 or newer. There is nothing to install.

cd rss_feed
npm start

Open http://127.0.0.1:4173 and paste a feed link into the box at the top of the sidebar. That's it.

npm stop        # stop the background server
npm run dev     # restart automatically while editing (Ctrl+C to quit)

npm start writes a PID file so npm stop can shut it down cleanly. If you start the server in a terminal instead, Ctrl+C works as usual.

Using Reader

Add a feed

Paste a feed URL, or just a site URL — Reader will look for the feed link on the page. Press Enter or the + button.

  • Direct feed: https://hnrss.org/frontpage
  • Site with autodiscovery: https://www.theverge.com/

If the site has no discoverable feed, Reader says so; find the RSS/Atom URL and paste that instead.

Read

Click a headline to open it in the reading pane. Opening an article marks it read. Open original opens the source page in a new tab.

Keep track

  • Unread shows just what you haven't read; the orange dot marks unread articles.
  • Starred is your saved list. Star from the list or the reading pane.
  • Mark all read clears the current view (feed + filter).
  • Search filters the current view as you type.

Remove a feed

Hover a feed, click the trash icon, then Remove. The row switches to an inline confirmation (Remove feed? [Remove] [Cancel]) — nothing is deleted until you confirm, and Esc cancels.

Refresh

  • ↻ next to “Feeds” refreshes everything.
  • Stale feeds refresh automatically every 10 minutes (and when the tab becomes visible again).
  • Failed feeds show a red ! on their avatar; hover for the error. One bad feed never blocks the others.

Keyboard shortcuts

Key Action
j / ↓ Next article
k / ↑ Previous article
m Toggle read / unread
s Toggle star
o Open original in a new tab
r Refresh all feeds
/ Focus search
Esc Close article / cancel confirmation / clear search

Shortcuts are ignored while you're typing in a field.

Configuration

Variable Default Purpose
PORT 4173 HTTP port
HOST 127.0.0.1 Interface to bind. Use 0.0.0.0 to reach it from other devices
DATA_DIR ./data Where the library is stored 
PORT=8080 HOST=0.0.0.0 npm start
PORT=8080 npm stop

Multiple libraries are just multiple data directories:

DATA_DIR=~/reading/work PORT=4174 node server.js

Your data

Everything lives in data/store.json:

  • the feeds you added,
  • a cache of their latest items,
  • which articles you've read or starred.

That file is written atomically (temp file + rename), so a crash won't corrupt it. It never leaves your machine; the only outbound traffic is fetching the feeds themselves.

To start over: npm stop and delete data/store.json. To back up, copy it.

How it works

        HTTP + JSON API              fetch()
browser ───────────────▶ server.js ───────────▶ RSS / Atom / JSON feeds
   ▲                        │
   └────────────────────────┴──────────▶ data/store.json
Path What it does
server.js HTTP server, JSON API, static files, feed fetching/caching, storage
lib/feed.js Normalizes RSS/RDF/Atom/JSON, discovers feeds, sanitizes article HTML
lib/xml.js A small XML parser (namespaces, CDATA, entities)
public/index.html Page structure
public/style.css Themes and responsive layout
public/app.js UI rendering, state, keyboard handling, API calls
scripts/stop.js PID-file based npm stop
data/store.json Your library (created on first run)

The server fetches a feed, parses it into one item shape regardless of format, stores the latest items, and serves them as JSON. The frontend is plain DOM code with no framework. Article HTML is stripped of scripts, iframes and event handlers, then rendered inside an iframe with sandbox (no allow-scripts), so feed content can't run code in the app.

API

Useful if you want to script the reader or build another client.

Method Path Purpose
GET /api/feeds Feeds, unread counts, totals
POST /api/feeds Add a feed: { "url": "https://…" }
DELETE /api/feeds/:id Remove a feed and its cached items
POST /api/feeds/:id/refresh Refresh one feed
POST /api/refresh Refresh all feeds
GET /api/items?filter=all|unread|starred&feed=:id&q= List articles
GET /api/items/:id One article, including content
POST /api/items/:id/read { "read": true }
POST /api/items/:id/star { "starred": true }
POST /api/read-all { "feed": "all", "filter": "unread" } 
curl -X POST localhost:4173/api/feeds \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"url":"https://hnrss.org/frontpage"}'

Troubleshooting

Problem What to do
“That page does not link to an RSS or Atom feed” The site hides its feed. Find the exact RSS/Atom URL and paste that.
“Server returned HTTP 403/419/…” The site blocks non-browser clients. Try a different feed URL or a mirror (e.g. hnrss.org instead of Hacker News' own /rss).
“Could not reach the server (ENOTFOUND/ECONNREFUSED)” Outbound network, DNS, proxy or firewall issue on the machine running Reader.
Feed loads but an article is empty The feed only publishes a short summary. Use Open original.
Port already in use PORT=8080 npm start (and PORT=8080 npm stop).
UI looks stale after an update Hard-refresh the tab (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+R).
A feed shows a red ! Hover it to see the error; the other feeds keep working. Fix the URL by removing and re-adding it.
Wrong feeds after experimenting npm stop, delete data/store.json, npm start.

Security and limitations

  • Local app, no authentication. Don't expose it to the internet as-is. If you need remote access, put it behind a reverse proxy with auth (and HTTPS).
  • The server will fetch whatever URL you give it, including internal addresses. Only run it for people you trust.
  • Article content is sanitized and sandboxed, but it is still third-party HTML. External images load from their original sites.
  • Single user, no sync, no full-text extraction, no offline images, no push.
  • No automated tests — verify changes against a couple of real feeds.

About

Reader was built in one sitting by DeepSeek (an AI model) from a short prompt asking for an RSS reader with a paste-a-link flow. The code is intentionally plain and readable so a human can audit or extend it. If you find rough edges, that's why.

If you build on it: the server is framework-free node:http, the frontend is vanilla DOM, and both are small enough to read in an afternoon.

License

Using Reader

Add a feed

Paste a feed URL, or just a site URL — Reader will look for the feed link on the page. Press Enter or the + button.

  • Direct feed: https://hnrss.org/frontpage
  • Site with autodiscovery: https://www.theverge.com/

If the site has no discoverable feed, Reader says so; find the RSS/Atom URL and paste that instead.

Read

Click a headline to open it in the reading pane. Opening an article marks it read. Open original opens the source page in a new tab.

Keep track

  • Unread shows just what you haven't read; the orange dot marks unread articles.
  • Starred is your saved list. Star from the list or the reading pane.
  • Mark all read clears the current view (feed + filter).
  • Search filters the current view as you type.

Remove a feed

Hover a feed, click the trash icon, then Remove. The row switches to an inline confirmation (Remove feed? [Remove] [Cancel]) — nothing is deleted until you confirm, and Esc cancels.

Refresh

  • ↻ next to “Feeds” refreshes everything.
  • Stale feeds refresh automatically every 10 minutes (and when the tab becomes visible again).
  • Failed feeds show a red ! on their avatar; hover for the error. One bad feed never blocks the others.

您的数据

Everything lives in data/store.json:

  • the feeds you added,
  • a cache of their latest items,
  • which articles you've read or starred.

That file is written atomically (temp file + rename), so a crash won't corrupt it. It never leaves your machine; the only outbound traffic is fetching the feeds themselves.

To start over: npm stop and delete data/store.json. To back up, copy it.

它是如何运作的

        HTTP + JSON API              fetch()
browser ───────────────▶ server.js ───────────▶ RSS / Atom / JSON feeds
   ▲                        │
   └────────────────────────┴──────────▶ data/store.json
Path 它的作用
server.js HTTP server, JSON API, static files, feed fetching/caching, storage
lib/feed.js Normalizes RSS/RDF/Atom/JSON, discovers feeds, sanitizes article HTML
lib/xml.js A small XML parser (namespaces, CDATA, entities)
public/index.html Page structure
public/style.css Themes and responsive layout
public/app.js UI rendering, state, keyboard handling, API calls
scripts/stop.js PID-file based npm stop
data/store.json Your library (created on first run)

The server fetches a feed, parses it into one item shape regardless of format, stores the latest items, and serves them as JSON. The frontend is plain DOM code with no framework. Article HTML is stripped of scripts, iframes and event handlers, then rendered inside an iframe with sandbox (no allow-scripts), so feed content can't run code in the app.

故障排除

问题 该怎么办
“That page does not link to an RSS or Atom feed” The site hides its feed. Find the exact RSS/Atom URL and paste that.
“Server returned HTTP 403/419/…” The site blocks non-browser clients. Try a different feed URL or a mirror (e.g. hnrss.org instead of Hacker News' own /rss).
“Could not reach the server (ENOTFOUND/ECONNREFUSED)” Outbound network, DNS, proxy or firewall issue on the machine running Reader.
Feed loads but an article is empty The feed only publishes a short summary. Use Open original.
Port already in use PORT=8080 npm start (and PORT=8080 npm stop).
UI looks stale after an update Hard-refresh the tab (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+R).
A feed shows a red ! Hover it to see the error; the other feeds keep working. Fix the URL by removing and re-adding it.
Wrong feeds after experimenting npm stop, delete data/store.json, npm start.

Security and limitations

  • Local app, no authentication. Don't expose it to the internet as-is. If you need remote access, put it behind a reverse proxy with auth (and HTTPS).
  • The server will fetch whatever URL you give it, including internal addresses. Only run it for people you trust.
  • Article content is sanitized and sandboxed, but it is still third-party HTML. External images load from their original sites.
  • Single user, no sync, no full-text extraction, no offline images, no push.
  • No automated tests — verify changes against a couple of real feeds.

About

Reader was built in one sitting by DeepSeek (an AI model) from a short prompt asking for an RSS reader with a paste-a-link flow. The code is intentionally plain and readable so a human can audit or extend it. If you find rough edges, that's why.

If you build on it: the server is framework-free node:http, the frontend is vanilla DOM, and both are small enough to read in an afternoon.
